questions.stem: At Fernway, the nightly pipeline copies 300 regions one at a time in a ForEach. How do you shorten it?

options.text: Split it into 300 pipelines run by hand
Add a Wait activity between iterations
Clear the ForEach's Sequential option and set a batch count, so iterations run in parallel
Increase the retry count

questions.explanation: A ForEach runs iterations in parallel unless Sequential is set; the batch count limits how many run at once.

questions.stem: Two Copy activities in a pipeline don't depend on each other, but one waits for the other to finish. How do you make them run at the same time?

options.text: Add a schedule
Turn on high concurrency
Put them in a ForEach with Sequential on
Remove the dependency between them so both start together

questions.explanation: Activities with no dependency between them run in parallel.

questions.stem: A Copy activity reads a very large table from a database that supports partitioned reads, and it's slow. What can speed it up?

options.text: Turn off the destination
Add a Wait activity
Use the source's partitioning option (an advanced setting some database connectors offer) so the copy reads in parallel
Copy the table one row at a time

questions.explanation: Partitioned reads let the Copy activity read slices of the table in parallel.

questions.stem: You want an on-demand copy of many small tables to finish faster with the least redesign. Which change usually helps most?

options.text: Copy each table twice
Run copies of independent tables in parallel instead of one after another
Add a notebook between every copy
Lower the pipeline's timeout

questions.explanation: Independent copies running in parallel use the time otherwise spent waiting. Extra steps only add time.

questions.stem: A Copy activity moves a large dataset and should use as much compute as the service can give it. Which intelligent throughput optimization option should you choose?

options.text: Balanced
Auto
Standard
Maximum

questions.explanation: Maximum lets the service apply throughput optimization using the maximum available compute. Standard and Balanced use fewer resources, and Auto lets the service decide.

questions.stem: You set a Copy activity's Degree of copy parallelism to 32, but the run used fewer parallel copies. Why?

options.text: The setting only applies when intelligent throughput optimization is Auto
The setting only applies inside a ForEach activity
The setting is ignored unless V-Order is turned on
The setting is a maximum, and at run time the copy uses a value less than or equal to it

questions.explanation: Degree of copy parallelism is the maximum number of threads; at run time the copy uses a value less than or equal to it. It's independent of intelligent throughput optimization.

questions.stem: A ForEach runs Copy activities for 200 tables in parallel, and the source database becomes overloaded. You want to keep some parallelism but limit it. What should you change?

options.text: Remove the Items expression from the ForEach
Increase each Copy activity's Degree of copy parallelism
Set the ForEach Batch count to a lower number
Select Sequential and set the Batch count to 200

questions.explanation: Batch count sets the maximum number of items processed at the same time when Sequential isn't selected. Sequential removes all parallelism, and higher copy parallelism adds load.

questions.stem: A ForEach with Sequential cleared contains three child activities: Lookup, Copy and Script. How does it run?

options.text: Items run one at a time, and the three child activities run in parallel
All child activities of all items start at the same time
Several items run in parallel, and for each item the three child activities run in order
Only the first child activity runs in parallel across items

questions.explanation: Without Sequential, multiple items run in parallel, but each item goes through the child activities in order.

questions.stem: A pipeline uses a Copy activity to move data from lakehouse tables into a warehouse in the same workspace. Which approach could be more performant and efficient?

options.text: Use CTAS or INSERT ... SELECT that reads the lakehouse table from the warehouse
Export the tables to CSV files and use a second Copy activity
Run singleton INSERT statements in a ForEach
Use a Dataflow Gen2 with staging disabled

questions.explanation: The warehouse guidance says CTAS or INSERT combined with SELECT FROM lakehouse tables or shortcuts could be more performant and efficient than pipelines. Singleton inserts create many small files.

questions.stem: Which two settings on a Copy activity's Settings tab can you change to improve its throughput? Each correct answer is a complete solution.

options.text: Sequential
Degree of copy parallelism
Retention
Intelligent throughput optimization
Batch count

questions.explanation: Intelligent throughput optimization and Degree of copy parallelism are Copy activity performance settings. Batch count and Sequential belong to ForEach, and retention belongs to other items.
